posts.title: 1950s Motorcycle Adventure: British Twins, Bandits and a Wild Ride Through India
posts.description: An exciting trip Touring in India in the 1950s brought up a host of challenges for an intrepid quintet on parallel twins. Appearing in the January 5, 1956, issue of The Motor Cycle, this picture was part of a report entitled ‘An Easter gallop’, which was accompanied by the subheading – with original capitals still in place – of: “Amusement and Stirring Adventure on a Round Trip from Calcutta to 4500ft Nettarhart”. It was written by Alan J D’Abreu, a photograph of whom was included on the first page. The accompanying picture for this piece was printed with the caption: “At Dumri – a country char shop – the four BSAs and the Triumphs come to rest. The author’s model faces the camera.” Expedition riding April 1956 The report starts by stating that Jack Wilks, an auctioneer and former Isle of Man TT racer, and one of the five-strong party, was going to be unable to travel with the group, as work commitments intervened. posts.title: George Brown: The Vincent Sprint King Who Chased 200mph
posts.description: The sprint king From Vincent employee to road racer to straight-line superstar, the name of George Brown will forever be linked with Vincent motorcycles. SIMON ROBINSON reports… It’s hard to imagine, these days, just how popular motorcycle sprinting was in the UK in the 1960s. A reasonable portion of this popularity was down to the actions of one man: George Brown. On his big Vincent twins, George chased records with a quiet confidence and an ever-optimistic charm. Sprinting wasn’t a sport that attracted attention-seekers. Sprinting was the work of dedication and grit. There were no big stadiums full of spectators, no champagne-drenched celebrations; instead, there was often a windswept runway on an old, abandoned airfield. These runways were about the only places in the UK that had sufficiently long straights to allow the taps on something like Brown’s Vincents to be fully opened, and George firmly believed that any records he set should be set on British soil. posts.title: Sammy Miller Motorcycle Museum Welcomes an Unexpected New Arrival
posts.description: The latest addition to the Sammy Miller Motorcycle Museum collection is certainly something a little different! Standing proudly in the Museum foyer is a life-size replica of an imposing Chinese Terracotta Warrior. If a trip to China to see the famous Terracotta Army isn’t on your itinerary, why not pop along to the Museum and see our very own warrior? He’s quite a character and makes a wonderful photo opportunity, so don’t forget your camera! Come and admire this magnificent warrior in all his glory! The world’s premier motorcycle museum Situated in the heart of the New Forest, the Sammy Miller Motorcycle Museum is home to around 500 rare and exotic motorcycles from all over the world.
